description:
FOUND s491 (Fable, 2026-09-19) while writing the #1912 review probe (its own reporting line `map { scalar(@$_) } \@a, \@b, â¦` printed wrong counts on main AND on the s491a tree); PRE-EXISTING on main 9e323b30, not caused by any open batch.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/s491a/p-backslash-list.pl and p-map-refs.pl (perl's answers are in the transcript of the task's filing; re-run both).
  my @a = (); my @b = (1, 2); my @c = ("x"); my %h = (k => 1);
  join ",", map { ref } \@a, \@b                      perl ARRAY,ARRAY      PCL  ","        (two empty strings: @b's elements, @a contributes none)
  join ",", map { scalar @$_ } \@b, \@c               perl 2,1              PCL  1,2,0      (the ELEMENTS 1, 2, "x" each taken as a symbolic array name)
  join ",", map { ref($_) } \%h, \@b                  perl HASH,ARRAY       PCL  HASH,,     (\%h is right; \@b is flattened)
  join ",", map { ref } \@a                           perl ARRAY            PCL  (empty)    (a SINGLE \@a too -- not a comma-precedence fact)
  join ",", map(ref, \@a, \@b)                        perl ARRAY,ARRAY      PCL  ","        (the paren/EXPR form of map as well)
  scalar(grep { ref } \@a, \@b)                       perl 2                PCL  0
  sort { @$a <=> @$b } \@b, \@a, \@c                  perl three refs       PCL  x,1,2
  my @p = map { [$_, scalar @$_] } \@b, \@c           perl 2 pairs          PCL  3
RIGHT on both: `map { â¦ } (\@a, \@b)` (parenthesised), `my @refs = (\@a, \@b); map { â¦ } @refs`, `push @l, \@a, \@b`, `cnt(\@a, \@b)`, `for my $r (\@a, \@b)`.

SO: the block-list operators' LIST operand path drops a leading `\` on an ARRAY operand (an array-flattening step -- the one that makes `map { } @a, @b` spread both arrays -- is applied to `\@b` as if it were `@b`), while the hash and scalar spellings survive.  It is not the comma/backslash precedence: a single `\@a` shows it.

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): `echo 'my @b=(1,2); my @r = map { ref } \@b;' | ./pl2cl` and read the map form's list operand -- is the emitted operand `@b` (the backslash dropped in PExpr's block-list argument handling / a `_flatten`-style normaliser that strips a refgen over an array) or `(p-backslash @b)` handed to a runtime `p-map` that flattens any raw vector it is given, including the VALUE of an array ref?  The second would be a box-model fact (an array ref's referent is the raw vector) and the fix is in how the list is built for the block-list macros, not in p-map.  The parenthesised spelling being right says the emission differs between the two spellings -- diff them.

WHY IT MATTERS: `map { â¦ } \@x, \@y` / `grep { â¦ } \@x, \@y` is the ordinary way to run one block over several arrays without copying them; the wrong answer is plausible-looking (element values instead of refs), not a crash.

WHERE (start): Pl/PExpr.pm's block-form list-operator argument path (the #153 / B2 region -- READ docs/pexpr-term-parsing-review.md FIRST and do not add guards to the $end_pars region) and Pl/ExprToCL.pm's map/grep/sort emitters; grep for where a `\` (refgen) node over an array operand is unwrapped.  CLAUDE.md rule 11: `map`/`grep`/`sort` are one family -- ONE fix upstream of all three, plus the EXPR form `map(EXPR, LIST)`.

BAR: Pl/ emission change -> corpus-diff (every differing file probed vs perl: a corpus site that moves was SILENTLY WRONG before), emission A/B over lib/**, gen bump + artifacts, full sweep, `--quick` companion once (op/grep.t, op/sort.t, op/list.t carry the shape); guard rows in Pl/t (a new map-grep-refs file or Pl/t/sort-01.t's sibling), inverse-verified.

=== DONE (s492a) ===
SHIPPED a0eaf8dc.  NOT PExpr/ExprToCL as filed -- the discriminating
measurement (diff the emission of `map { ref } \@b` against the parenthesised
spelling) showed the emission is already right and byte-identical.  The bug is
in the RUNTIME collectors: they unboxed each item before asking "is this a
vector to spread?", and `p-backslash` of an array is exactly a p-box holding a
vector, so the referent was flattened.

ONE predicate now, `%p-spread-vector-p` -- a RAW non-string vector is an
array's live storage and spreads; a vector inside a p-box is a REFERENCE and is
one element -- read by `%p-collect-list` (p-map / p-grep / p-sort / p-reverse),
`%p-sort-collect-plain` and `p-join`.  `p-flatten-args` (the @_ builder) always
read it that way, which is why `f(\@a,\@b)` was never affected (rule 11: the
sibling was right).

WIDER THAN FILED: `reverse \@a,\@b`, `join ",", \@a`, `join ",", $hashref` and
every ARRAY-REF VALUE handed to one of them (`map { ref } $h->{list}` gave
three empty strings).  35-row table probed vs perl 5.40.3, identical after
(scratch/s492a/probes/m2-family.{pl,perl.out,base.out,tree.out}).

Guard Pl/t/listop-refs-01.t (6 rows; rows 1-3 FAIL on a 268d7e00 extraction,
4-6 -- the spreading and aliasing the fix must not break -- pass).
Sweep TOTAL 18687 -> 18689 (+2): perl-tests/join.t's two GH #21484 rows assert
that an overloaded `""` among join's arguments is stringified, and p-join used
to SPREAD the blessed hash ref into nothing.  Both baselines edited row by row;
two now-stale cl/skip-registry.lisp entries removed.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): in the argument list of `map` / `grep` / `sort`, `\@array` LOSES ITS BACKSLASH and the array is FLATTENED -- `map { scalar @$_ } \@b` iterates @b's ELEMENTS (perl: one array ref), `map { ref } \@a, \@b` answers empty strings, `sort { @$a <=> @$b } \@x, \@y` sorts the elements; `\%h` and `\$s` in the same list are right, and so are `push @l, \@a, \@b`, `f(\@a, \@b)`, `for (\@a, \@b)` and the PARENTHESISED list `map { â¦ } (\@a, \@b)`
